Building and publishing packages¶

The project builds a pure-Python wheel and source distribution. CI checks formatting, tests, documentation, metadata, and installed-wheel execution. The publishing workflow also installs and runs the sdist before uploading. Version tags trigger publication; manual publication from main is available.

From a clean checkout:

uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra docs --extra release
uv run --locked black --check .
uv run --locked python -m pytest -q -W error::RuntimeWarning --cov --cov-report=xml
uv run --locked python -m sphinx -b html -W --keep-going docs build/manual
uv build --no-sources
uv run --locked --extra release python -m twine check --strict dist/*

Use an empty dist/ directory for each release so old artifacts cannot be uploaded accidentally. Install both distributions in fresh environments outside the checkout, check imports and poly-mpm modern_ball, and inspect the rendered package description. A full example produces output; use a temporary directory. CI checks the wheel; the publishing workflow checks both the wheel and sdist.

Trusted Publishing workflow¶

.github/workflows/pypi.yml builds, checks, and publishes using PyPI Trusted Publishing. The configured publisher uses benjym/poly-mpm, workflow pypi.yml, and no GitHub environment. The publishing job deliberately has no environment field so its OIDC identity matches that configuration. Only that job receives id-token: write; it downloads the tested distributions without checking out or executing project source. No API token is required.

Publish a version tag¶

  1. Set the intended version in pyproject.toml, run uv lock, and commit/push the tested source to main. Inspect metadata, package contents and README links before tagging. Every published version must be unique.

  2. Create an annotated tag matching that version and push it. For example, after setting the project version to 1.0.1:

    git tag -a v1.0.1 -m "Release poly-mpm 1.0.1"
git push origin refs/tags/v1.0.1

  3. The tag push starts Publish to PyPI. Tags matching v[0-9]* trigger the workflow, and its version check requires the exact name v<project version>. The checked-out source, tests, distributions and published package all come from that tagged commit. A mismatched tag fails before publication.

  4. After success, verify installation from PyPI and add release notes for the tag.

Pushing ordinary commits to main runs CI without publishing. Creating a GitHub release for an already-pushed tag does not start another upload. PyPI versions cannot be overwritten: increment the version and create a new tag for a new release.

Manual publication¶

Open Actions → Publish to PyPI → Run workflow, select main, and enter the exact version from pyproject.toml. The workflow runs the same checks before uploading. Manual dispatch on another branch is skipped. Use this option for an intentional release without a new tag; do not dispatch an already-published version. A pending publisher becomes active after its first successful upload.

The publisher uses production PyPI. A TestPyPI rehearsal requires a separately configured publisher and destination. If you add a protected GitHub environment later, update both the publisher and workflow to the same environment name.

See PyPI Trusted Publishing for the OIDC identity requirements. CODECOV_TOKEN is used only by coverage CI and provides no package-publishing access.
